text: AI is changing our world quickly, and many experts predict that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, could arrive within the next few decades. Unlike today’s narrow AI, which handles specific tasks like translation or image recognition, AGI would match human ability across all mental work. The potential benefits are huge: AGI could help cure diseases, solve climate problems, and boost education for everyone. However, risks exist too, including job loss, privacy invasion, and even misuse by bad actors. Some thinkers say we should slow down research until we create safety rules. Others believe the timeline is uncertain—maybe 10 years, maybe 50. Either way, careful planning and open discussion will shape whether AGI becomes our greatest tool or our biggest challenge.
